podcast.body: Released at the end of the 1970s, this song about "being a hooker" is mentioned as part of a trend of women in music claiming ownership over their own sexuality, alongside LaBelle's "Lady Marmalade." "Do songs about being a hooker like this one that was released in 1974 or Bad Girls, which was released at the end of the 70s, do they count as women claiming their own sexuality?"

This song rose to number one on the charts during the week ending July 14, 1979, becoming one of two of Donna Summer's singles in the top three in America at that time. It was the title track of her chart-topping double album *Bad Girls*. "when the song Bad Girls rose to number one."

podcast.body: This song was the winner of the 1979 Billboard Song of the Summer and topped the 70s ranking. Donna Summer had a dominant summer, scoring back-to-back number ones in June and July that both made the top five of Billboard's tally. "Bad Girls," the follow-up to "Hot Stuff," was equally "steamy" and explicitly addressed sex workers applying their trade, making its win fitting given her surname. "For crying out loud, summer was her last name. So it's only right that bad girls. 1979's song of the summer tops my 70s ranking."
